children: Gold hovers above the key $4,000 mark as markets await a raft of central bank decisions headlined by the Federal Reserve. With the Fed tipped to hold, focus is on any signaling on when the next rate hike might come as oil prices stay elevated and inflation high. A more hawkish tone would likely weigh on the non-interest-bearing metal. Fed Chair Warsh has made it clear he's not big on forward guidance, so traders will take cues from U.S. growth and inflation data too. The big unknown is once again the dollar, which continues to rebound, says Trade Nation's David Morrison. For now, gold seems to be consolidating, he says. Gold is up 0.3% at $4,068/oz. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
